senses.gloss:
हिम हिम, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s.
I. 146. fr. हि substituted for rt. 1. हन्; according
to others from a lost rt. ह्यम्), cold, frigid, frosty,
icy, dewy, any cold substance; (अस्), m. the cold season,
cold, winter (= हेमन्त, p. 1173); the moon;
the Himālaya mountain; the sandal tree; camphor;
(आ), f. the cold season, winter; a year (Ved.); small
cardamoms; a variety of the fragrant grass Cyperus
(= भद्र-मुस्ता, नागर-मुस्ता); a kind of plant
(= पृक्का); a kind of grass (= चणिका); the fra-
grant drug and perfume Reṇukā; (अम्), n. frost,
hoar-frost, ice, snow, dew, cold, coldness, coolness,
(in Ṛg-veda X. 37, 10. हिमा, inst. c. = शैत्येन,
and thought by some to come from a monosyllabic
form हिम्); night, (in Naigh. I. 7. हिमा, inst. c.
is enumerated among the रात्रि-नामानि; cf. हिम्या
under हिम्य); sandal-wood; another fragrant wood
(of cooling properties, = पद्म-काष्ठ); fresh
butter; tin; a pearl; a lotus; [cf. Zend zjao, zim,
zima, ‘winter:’ Gr. χι-ών (χίον-ος), δύσ-χιμο-ς,
χεῖ-μα, χειμάζω, χειμαίνω, χίμεθλο-ν, χειμών,
χειμερινό-ς: Lat. hiem-s, hibernu-s (for himer-
nus): Slav. zima, ‘winter:’ Lith. zema, zemini-s:
Hib. geimhre, geimhrith, geimhreadh, ‘winter;’
gamh, ‘winter, cold.’]
—हिम-कर, अस्, ई, अम्,
causing or producing cold, frigorific, cold; (अस्), m.
the moon; camphor.
—हिम-कूट, अस्, m. ‘cold-
[]
summit,’ the winter season.
—हिम-गर्भ, अस्, आ,
अम्, laden with snow.
—हिम-गिरि, इस्, m. the Himālaya
mountain.
—हिम-गु, उस्, m. ‘cold-rayed,’ epithet
of the moon; [cf. शीत-गु.]
—हिम-गौर, अस्, आ,
अम्, white as snow.
—हिम-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced
by cold; born or produced in the Himālaya mountain;
(अस्), m. the mountain Maināka; (आ), f. ‘daughter
of Himālaya;’ the plant called Zedoary; another
plant (= क्षीरिणी); Pārvatī.
—हिम-ज्झटि, इस्, f.
(ज्झटि for झटि, see rt. झट्), ‘intermixture of cold
dew,’ hoar-frost, mist, fog; [cf. कु-ज्झटि.]
—हिम-
ज्वर, अस्, m. fever with cold paroxysms, ague.
—हिम-तैल, अम्, n. a kind of camphor ointment.
—हिम-दीधिति, इस्, m. ‘having cool rays,’ the
moon.
—हिम-दुग्धा, f. ‘having cool juice,’ a kind
of milky plant or tree (= क्षीरिणी).
—हिम-दुर्-
दिन, अम्, n. cold and bad weather, frosty or snowy
weather, wintry weather.
—हिम-द्युति, इस्, m.
‘having cool radiance,’ the moon.
—हिम-द्रुम,
अस्, m. a sort of large Nimba tree.
—हिम-द्रुह्,
ध्रुक्, m. ‘dew-dispeller,’ the sun.
—हिम-धातु,
उस्, m. ‘having cold minerals,’ the Himālaya moun-
tain.
—हिम-ध्वस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, withered by cold,
frost-bitten, frost-nipt (as a lotus &c.).
—हिम-
निर्मुक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, freed from frost.
—हिम-
प्रस्थ, अस्, m. ‘having snowy table-land,’ the
Himālaya mountain.
—हिम-बालुक, अस्, आ, m. f.
camphor.
—हिम-भास्, आस्, m. ‘having cool lustre,’
epithet of the moon.
—हिम-रश्मि, इस्, m. ‘having
cool rays,’ the moon.
—हिमरश्मि-ज, अस्, m.
‘born from the moon,’ epithet of the planet Budha
or Mercury.
—हिमर्तु (˚म-ऋतु), उस्, m. the cold
season.
—हिम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having frost or
snow, snowy, frosty, icy, freezing, snow-clad; (आन्),
m. the Himālaya mountain or the Himālaya per-
sonified, (see हिमालय.)
—हिमवत, at the end of
a comp. = हिम-वत् above.
—हिमवत्-कुक्षि,
इस्, m. a valley of the Himālaya.
—हिमवत्-खण्ड,
N. of a book of the Skanda-Purāṇa.
—हिम-
वत्-प्रभव, अस्, आ, अम्, springing from or be-
longing to the Himālaya mountain.
—हिमवत्-
सुत, अस्, m. ‘son of the Himālaya,’ the moun-
tain Maināka; (आ), f. the Ganges; Pārvatī.
—हिम-
वद्-गिरि, इस्, m. a snowy mountain.
—हिमवद्-
गिरि-संश्रय, अस्, m. ‘taking refuge in the Himā-
laya mountain,’ epithet of Śiva.
—हिम-विद्ध,
अस्, आ, अम्, ‘frost-pierced,’ penetrated with frost (as
the west wind in the cold season).
—हिम-शर्करा,
f. a kind of sugar (= यावनाली).
—हिम-शीतल, अस्,
आ, अम्, very cold or frosty, freezing.
—हिम-शुचि-
भस्म-भूषित, अस्, आ, अम्, adorned with ashes
white as snow.
—हिम-शैल, अस्, m. a snowy moun-
tain, the Himālaya.
—हिमशैल-जा, f. ‘daughter
of Himālaya,’ the goddess Durgā or Pārvatī.
—हिम-
श्रथ, अस्, m. ‘shedding cold,’ the moon.
—हिम-
संहति, इस्, f. a mass of ice or snow.
—हिम-
सरस्, अस्, n. cold water.
—हिम-हान-कृत्, त्, m.
‘causing loss of cold,’ fire.
—हिम-हासक, अस्, m.
‘winter-smiler,’ the marshy date tree.
—हिमांशु
(˚म-अं˚), उस्, m. ‘cool-rayed,’ the moon; camphor.
—हिमांश्व्-अभिख्य, अम्, n. ‘called after the
moon,’ silver.
—हिमागम (˚म-आग्˚), अस्, m. ‘ap-
proach of cold,’ the cold season, winter.
—हिमाद्रि
(˚म-अद्˚), इस्, m. a snowy range of mountains, the
Himālaya mountain (sometimes personified).
—हिमा-
द्रि-जा, f. ‘daughter of Himālaya,’ Pārvatī; a kind of
plant or tree (= क्षीरिणी).
—हिमाद्रि-तनया, f.
‘daughter of Himālaya,’ Durgā.
—हिमाद्रि-तनया-
पति, इस्, m. ‘husband of the daughter of Himā-
laya,’ Śiva.
—हिमानिल (˚म-अन्˚), अस्, m. a cold
or frosty wind.
—हिमाब्ज (˚म-अब्˚), अम्, n. a
lotus.
—हिमाभ (˚म-आभ), अस्, आ, अम्, resem-
bling cold, like snow or frost.
—हिमाम्बु (˚म-
अम्˚), उ, n. cold water.
—हिमाराति (˚म-अर्˚), इस्, m.
‘enemy of cold,’ fire; the sun; a kind of plant (=
चित्रक); another plant (= अर्क).
—हिमारुण
(˚म-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, grey with frost.
—हिमार्त
(˚म-आर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, pinched with cold, suffering from
cold, chilled, frozen.
—हिमार्दित (˚म-अर्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, pinched or pained by cold.
—हिमालय (˚म-
आल्˚), अस्, m. ‘abode of snow,’ the Himālaya range of
[]
mountains (which bounds India on the north and
separates it from Tartary, giving rise to the rivers
Ganges and Indus, and containing the highest eleva-
tions in the world; in mythology personified as the
husband of Menā or Menakā, by whom he had a
son called Maināka, who is also a personified moun-
tain; he was moreover the father of Durgā or Umā,
who became incarnate as Pārvatī, ‘daughter of the
Mountain,’ to captivate Śiva and withdraw him from
a severe penance he had undertaken to perform in
the region of Himālaya; the personified Mountain
is also represented as the father of Gaṅgā, who, as the
personified Ganges, is generally regarded as his eldest
daughter, though sometimes identified with Pārvatī);
the white Khadira tree; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= भू-
म्य्-आमलकी).
—हिमालय-सुता, f. ‘daughter of
Himālaya,’ Umā or Pārvatī.
—हिमा-वती, f. a kind
of Soma or moon-plant (= स्वर्ण-क्षीरी, q. v.).
—हिमाश्रया (˚म-आश्˚), f. ‘depending on cold,’
a kind of plant (= स्वर्ण-जीवन्ती).
—हिमाह्व
(˚म-आह्˚), अस्, m. ‘called after ice,’ camphor.
—हिमाह्वय (˚म-आह्˚), अस्, m. ‘called after ice,’
camphor; (अम्), n. a lotus.
—हिमोत्तरा (˚म-उत्˚), f.
‘following on cold,’ the tawny grape.
—हिमोत्पन्न
(˚म-उत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, produced by cold; (आ), f. a
kind of sugar (= यावनाली).
—हिमोद्भवा (˚म-
उद्˚), f. ‘cold-produced,’ the plant called Zedoary
(= शटी).
—हिमोस्र (˚म-उस्˚), अस्, m. ‘cool-
rayed,’ epithet of the moon.
हिमा, f. See under हिम, p. 1172.

हिमक, अस्, m. a kind of tree (= वि-कङ्कत);
N. of a prince or chief of Kaśmīra.
हिमवल, अम्, n. (also read हेमवल), a pearl.

हिमानी, f. great frost, a mass of snow, collection
of ice and snow (= हिम-संहति), snow-drift; a
kind of sugar (= यावनाली).
—हिमानी-विशद, अस्,
आ, अम्, white as a snow-drift.

हिमेलु, उस्, उस्, उ, chilly, suffering from cold,
frozen.

हिम्न, अस्, m. (see 1. हेमन् and हेम्ना below),
the planet Mercury.

हिम्य, अस्, आ, अम्, frosty, snowy, icy, dewy, cold,
frigid, (in Ṛg-veda I. 34, 1. हिम्या, ‘with the night,’
is explained by Sāy. as = हिम-युक्तया रात्र्या,
‘with the frosty night.’)
